Widgets and complications

Adding a widget

  • iPhone and iPad: touch and hold the Home Screen or Lock Screen, tap Edit or Customize, then Add Widget, and search for TianganDizhi. Home Screen widgets come in small, medium, large and extra-large sizes.
  • Apple Watch: touch and hold the watch face, tap Edit, and choose a TianganDizhi complication.
  • Mac: the menu bar shows the current Shichen and date. Click it to copy the details.

Tap a widget to jump straight to its solar term, festival or almanac details.

A widget looks out of date

iOS and watchOS decide when widgets refresh. Opening TianganDizhi once brings them up to date. If a widget still looks wrong, remove it and add it again.

Calendar and time

Festivals fall on a different day than in China

Outside UTC+8, a festival or solar term can start on a different local date. To use China's dates, turn on 節日與節氣使用東八區時間 (festivals and solar terms use UTC+8) under 地區與日曆 in Settings.

Traditional names, fonts and themes

In Settings you can:

  • show the traditional, classical names for the Shichen and solar terms (顯示傳統名稱)
  • use the system font instead of the Weibei calligraphy font (使用系統字體)
  • give widgets a red background during the Spring Festival (組件紅底)

The app is available in English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese, and follows your device's language.

Adding my own festivals

In the upcoming festivals list, choose 添加自訂節日 (add a custom festival) to add your own dates.

Sunrise, sunset and the moon

Sunrise, sunset, moonrise and moonset come from Apple WeatherKit and use your location, if you allow it. If you don't, the app shows approximate times. To change this, go to Settings › Privacy & Security › Location Services › TianganDizhi.

Privacy

TianganDizhi has no accounts and no ads. On iPhone and iPad it sends anonymous usage statistics, and you can turn them off any time in the app: Settings (設定) → Privacy (隱私) → Allow anonymous usage statistics (允許匿名使用統計). The privacy policy has the details.
